description: Baseline: streaming Keylock engine quality benchmark (real music 40s slow/fast/identity/ride + sine ride). quality=81.87

asi.biggest_levers: transient_f1 fast render 0.489 (smearing on speedup); identity_corr 0.505 at rate 1.0 (keylock chain not transparent)

description: Harness calibration (not a DSP change): compensate reported pipeline latency in transient F1, phase-blind identity metric (LR8 allpass), add hard ±14-16% ratios. New effective baseline 95.34.

asi.hypothesis: harness had latency bias + phase-sensitive identity metric
asi.finding: transient_f1 0.61->0.92 purely from latency compensation; identity xcorr 0.50 was allpass phase, spectral sim is 0.991
asi.levers: spec_sim slow2 (-16%) = 0.916 worst; transient_f1 ~0.92 all rates

description: SOLA TRANSIENT_POSTPONE_RATIO 3.0→1.8: postpone splices near weaker energy bursts. transient_f1 0.9188→0.9210, tiny but real (deterministic bench).

asi.hypothesis: more conservative online transient postpone protects more attacks
asi.result: +0.066 quality via transient_f1 +0.0022; small because postpone only delays, doesn't relocate splices
asi.next: try shorter/longer XFADE, DRIFT_TRIGGER, or outgoing-span energy check

description: DRIFT_TRIGGER 192→128 + HARD 320→256: more frequent smaller splices. Worse everywhere: spec −0.0014, transient −0.0023, pitch p95 0.43→0.71c.

asi.hypothesis: smaller more frequent splices reduce per-splice damage
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.41→94.76; more splices = more fades = more pitch wobble and more attack smears
asi.next_action_hint: try the opposite: LARGER drift trigger (fewer splices), e.g. 256/384

description: DRIFT_TRIGGER 192→256 + HARD 320→448: fewer larger splices. Also worse: transient_f1 0.921→0.902, pitch 0.43→0.55c. 192/320 is a local optimum.

asi.hypothesis: fewer larger splices = less total fade damage
asi.rollback_reason: quality 95.41→94.63; larger jumps skip/repeat more audio per splice, hurting transients (0.921→0.902)
asi.learning: DRIFT/HARD trigger 192/320 is locally optimal in both directions; stop tuning it
asi.next_action_hint: focus on splice PLACEMENT (online onset detection feeding OnsetEvents) instead of splice frequency

description: Online onset detection at SOLA ingest (RMS jump 2.5x, refractory 46ms) feeding both splice protection and masked-window placement. transient_f1 0.921→0.910 — worse.

asi.hypothesis: online attack detection at ingest (~13ms lookahead) protects transients from splice fades
asi.suspect: masked-window opportunistic splices now fire 17-46ms AFTER each detected kick — inside the kick body/decay — smearing it; or postponed splices get forced at HARD_TRIGGER in worse spots
asi.next_action_hint: retry with online onsets used for span PROTECTION only (not masked-window placement)

description: Online onset detection, protection-only variant (no masked-window use). Still worse than baseline: transient_f1 0.921→0.915.

asi.hypothesis: online onsets for fade-span protection only
asi.learning: onset protection postpones splices past DRIFT_TRIGGER; the forced splices at HARD_TRIGGER are then LARGER jumps, which experiment #4/#5 showed hurt more than fade-through-transient does. The existing energy-postpone (1.8x) already covers the useful cases
asi.next_action_hint: stop onset-protection direction; attack transient smearing differently — e.g. splice landing refinement, or XFADE shape/length
